title: Customer-scoped canary eval channels with encrypted artifact handling
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce customer-scoped canary evaluation channels that run private, per-customer eval suites whenever a model binary, quantization profile, or serving config is changed in Dedicated/Private deployments. Eval artifacts (datasets, logs, results) must be encrypted at rest and scoped so that tenant data never leaves the customer boundary. The feature should allow opt-in/opt-out, configurable eval frequency, and clearly surfaced pass/fail signals to the Redwood Console and to customer webhooks.
acceptance_criteria: A per-customer canary eval pipeline can be enabled per Dedicated/Private customer with a simple toggle in the Console and via the API
Eval runs are triggered automatically on model version, quantization profile, or runtime config changes; configurable throttle to avoid resource exhaustion
All eval artifacts are stored with customer-specific encryption keys (KMS or customer-managed HSM) and access controls that prevent cross-tenant leakage
Console shows a canary status: last run timestamp, pass/fail, top regressions, and a link to sanitized diffs
Customers can subscribe to webhook notifications for regression failures and optionally approve/rollback model rollouts
E2E tests validate that a seeded private dataset used for a customer eval never appears in shared logs or telemetry
Feature works in both Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with the same API surface
notes: Motivation: customers operating in regulated industries want deterministic regression checks tied to any change that could affect model output quality. Current global eval pipelines are insufficient for tenant isolation and compliance audits.

Trade-offs discussed: running full eval suites per customer uses more compute and increases costs. Proposed hybrid approach: lightweight smoke tests + periodic full-suite runs; allow customers to configure intensity.
Privacy design: use ephemeral staging buckets inside customer VPC for Private installs; for Dedicated we will provision per-tenant encrypted object prefixes with separate KMS keys.
Rollout plan: start with a pilot group (3 enterprise customers) on Dedicated, then extend to Private packages in 2 phases after security audit
Metrics to track: eval cost per customer, false positive rate of regressions, time from config change to canary result, number of auto-rollbacks triggered
